section_summary: This section concludes a SCAP study of Japan’s cotton textile industry, covering spindle rehabilitation, raw cotton supplies, exports, domestic allocation and production limits. It includes the directives cited by the study, a January 1947 staff study, statistical tables and footnote references. Later correspondence concerns selling Japanese textiles abroad, sharing a State Department report, and the effect of Japanese competition on U.S. textile interests.

subfiles.title: Cotton industry rehabilitation program: concluding sections
subfiles.from: SCAP Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: Reviews implementation of the four-million-spindle limit and prospects for Japanese cotton production, exports and domestic supply.
subfiles.summary: The study traces SCAP directives, loans and limits on the Big Ten spinning companies. It finds that shortages of materials, labor, power and raw cotton constrain rehabilitation and output. It projects production and cotton needs for 1948–49, argues that export sales are needed to finance imports, and describes inadequate domestic supplies and corrective action against weavers withholding cloth.

subfiles.title: Financial Plan for Rehabilitation of the Cotton Industry in Japan
subfiles.from: SCAP General Headquarters
subfiles.about: Conditionally permits a 600-million-yen rehabilitation loan.
subfiles.summary: Permits initial borrowing, subject to company applications, spending limits and monthly plant reports.

subfiles.title: Cotton Textile Capacity
subfiles.from: SCAP General Headquarters; John B. Cooley
subfiles.about: Approves rebuilding to four million cotton spindles and complementary equipment.
subfiles.summary: Sets the four-million-spindle capacity level without granting material or fuel priorities.

subfiles.title: Limitation on Size of Spinning Companies
subfiles.from: SCAP General Headquarters; R. G. Hersey for John B. Cooley
subfiles.about: Limits the Big Ten companies to their inventoried spindle holdings.
subfiles.summary: Lists each company’s allotment, cancels its outstanding orders for new spinning machinery, and reserves future machinery production for independent firms.

subfiles.title: Cotton Textile Capacity
subfiles.from: H. S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Directs invitations for independent firms to apply for spindle capacity.
subfiles.summary: Orders applications from existing independent spinners and public invitations for remaining authorized capacity.

subfiles.title: Limitation on Size of Spinning Companies
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Corrects the inventory date in SCAPIN 1562.
subfiles.summary: Changes the Big Ten inventory date to January 31, 1947.

subfiles.title: Cotton Textile Capacity
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Defines maximum spindle operation under SCAPIN 1512.
subfiles.summary: Defines maximum operation as two normal shifts of eight and a half hours each day.

subfiles.title: Cotton Textile Capacity
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Revises instructions for independent spinners’ capacity applications.
subfiles.summary: Broadens invitations to independent owners and revises the capacity available beyond the Big Ten allotment.

subfiles.title: Limitation on Size of Spinning Companies
subfiles.from: SCAP General Headquarters; R. G. Hersey for R. L. Levy
subfiles.about: Amends the restriction on new spinning machinery orders.
subfiles.summary: Reserves future machinery production for firms unaffiliated with or uncontrolled by the listed Big Ten companies.

subfiles.title: Limitation on Size of Spinning Companies
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Defines cotton spinning spindles and revises Big Ten allotments.
subfiles.summary: Excludes specified waste-processing spindles from the cotton-spindle definition and reduces five companies’ allotments by 21,652 spindles. It gives revised Big Ten totals and directs reallocation of the excluded capacity.

subfiles.title: Limitation on Size of Spinning Companies
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Amends the rule for reallocating 21,652 spindles.
subfiles.summary: Directs the released capacity to concerns outside the listed Big Ten companies.

subfiles.title: Cotton Industry Regulations
subfiles.from: Harold S. Tate, SCAP Textile Division
subfiles.to: Textile Bureau, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Approves proposed regulations for cotton spinning rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Approves the Textile Bureau’s submitted rehabilitation regulations.

subfiles.title: Action Taken on Central Liaison Office Memorandum
subfiles.from: SCAP General Headquarters; M. F. Moyes for R. L. Levy
subfiles.about: Permits ten companies to borrow additional rehabilitation funds.
subfiles.summary: Allows a 718,954,280-yen loan for spinning and weaving mills, with progress and accounting reports required.

subfiles.title: Interim Level of Japanese Cotton-Textile Production
subfiles.from: F. Marquat, Chief, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: Recommends four million spindles as Japan’s interim cotton textile capacity.
subfiles.summary: Estimates domestic consumer and industrial needs alongside likely exports, then calculates the spindle capacity needed to meet them. It recommends a four-million-spindle goal, gradual expansion and integration with wider resource allocations.

subfiles.title: Statistical Tables I–XI
subfiles.from: SCAP Economic and Scientific Section; textile association sources
subfiles.about: Compiles historical and projected figures for Japanese cotton capacity, production and export destinations.
subfiles.summary: The tables show rehabilitation plans; annual and monthly spindle, loom, yarn and fabric figures; and prewar and postwar cotton yarn and fabric exports by destination. They draw chiefly on Japanese textile association statistics.

subfiles.title: Footnote References
subfiles.from: SCAP Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: Lists directives and statistical sources cited in the cotton program.
subfiles.summary: Identifies cited SCAP memoranda and textile statistics sources.

subfiles.title: Japanese Textile Sales
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Secretary of the Army
subfiles.about: Urges State Department support for selling accumulated Japanese textile exports.
subfiles.summary: Royall explains the dollar repayment problem created by a new raw-material revolving fund, reports sales initiatives and prospective sterling-area negotiations, and suggests briefing officers before a Far East commercial conference.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Sadek Ibrahim Correspondence
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Cairo
subfiles.about: Forwards Ibrahim’s request and the Department’s reply.
subfiles.summary: Sends both letters to Cairo for discretionary delivery.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese Cotton Textile Industry Reports
subfiles.from: Sadek Ibrahim
subfiles.to: Manager, Office of Intelligence Research, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests reports for an Arabic book on textiles.
subfiles.summary: Ibrahim asks for the report on Japanese cotton textile capabilities and other textile reports; page 165 is another copy.

subfiles.title: Reply to Sadek Ibrahim
subfiles.from: John H. Ottemiller, Department of State
subfiles.about: Supplies the requested Japanese cotton textile industry report.
subfiles.summary: Encloses OIR Report No. 4389-R for Ibrahim’s use.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of OIR Report No. 4786
subfiles.from: Office of Intelligence Research
subfiles.about: Summarizes a study of Japanese textile expansion and its effect on U.S. cotton trade.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum says six million Japanese spindles would require about 2.5 million bales of cotton, perhaps half from the United States. It expects Japan to regain Asian and African textile markets and judges that extra U.S. raw cotton sales could outweigh additional losses in U.S. fabric exports.

subfiles.title: Meeting with Representatives of the U.S. Textile Industry
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley
subfiles.about: Records discussion of a proposed joint textile mission to Japan and access to sterling-area markets.
subfiles.summary: Industry representatives consider a joint mission, market shares and a protest over British trade practices.

subfiles.title: Japanese Trade Competition with American Interests
subfiles.from: Mr. Stolle
subfiles.about: Requests an assessment of Japanese textile competition against U.S. raw cotton sales.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a concise study balancing prospective U.S. raw cotton gains against textile export losses.
